sections.h2: What makes Twiggs County different from its neighbors?
sections.html:
Twiggs County calls itself the geographic center of Georgia, and the claim has a marker behind it. State geologists and the U.S. Geological Survey placed the center in a swampy spot where Turvin and Savage creeks meet, near the old first county seat of Marion. The legislature passed the bill creating the county on December 14, 1809, carving it from Wilkinson County and naming it for a Revolutionary War major general.

The county covers about 360 square miles. Its north end rolls like the Piedmont, while the south has the flat pine woods of south Georgia. It lies along the Fall Line, which brought kaolin; that clay industry, with forestry and farming, carried the economy through the 1900s. Interstate 16 runs through the middle, linking Macon and Savannah, and two industrial parks of 150 and 500 acres sit where I-16 meets Highway 96.

Jeffersonville is the present county seat. Its courthouse dates to 1902 and 1903 and was renovated in 1979, then expanded in the 1990s and early 2000s, according to the county's own site.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about owning a home in Twiggs County?
sections.html:
Twiggs is a county of owners: 88.2% of housing units are owner-occupied for 2020 to 2024, and the median value is $111,300. Population is the other story, since the 2025 estimate of 7,597 is 5.4% below the 2020 base of 8,028.

Only 13 building permits were issued in 2025, and 96.1% of residents stayed in the same house for a year. Density is 22.3 people per square mile. Many parcels here are acreage, timber or family land passed down, which suits a seller who needs a fast, as-is closing more than a showing schedule.

sections.h2: Where do I go for Twiggs County property tax questions?
sections.html:
Three offices sit in the courthouse at 425 Railroad Street in Jeffersonville, and each does a different job.

  • Tax commissioner, (478) 945-3359, P.O. Box 187: pays property tax, motor vehicle tax, tags and titles.
  • Board of Tax Assessors and Chief Appraiser, Room 102, (478) 945-3663, P.O. Box 111: values, returns, homestead, current-use and forest land exemptions, and appeals.
  • County commissioners: set the budget and the county share of the millage rate.

The assessors meet on the first Thursday of each month at 9:00 a.m. in Room 102, and the office takes walk-ins from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. A field appraiser carrying identification and driving a marked county vehicle may visit a parcel to verify data tied to an appeal, a return, a permit or a sales check. A notice announcing the 2026 tax digest and five-year levy history was posted on August 21, 2026.

sections.h2: What is the due date and late penalty in Twiggs County?
sections.html:
Read the due date on your own bill. Georgia's default is December 20, but the Department of Revenue says a county may move it to December 1 or November 15, or split billing into installments, so the Twiggs tax commissioner is the authority on yours.

State rules give each taxpayer 60 days from the postmark of the bill before interest begins, and unpaid balances can also draw penalties. Call (478) 945-3359 and ask for the exact date, the interest rate in effect and the payoff on any past-due year. If you own a mobile home, ask separately, because the state's mobile home permit and return run on a January 1 to April 1 cycle.

  • Refund requests for taxes wrongly assessed must begin within three years of payment.
  • Municipal tax in some counties is billed by the city clerk, so ask whether a city bill also applies.

sections.h2: How does a Twiggs County valuation appeal work?
sections.html:
Assessment notices go out in late May or early June, and you have 45 days from the date on the notice. File by mail with a letter or the state form; the letter should carry your parcel ID, the property address, a daytime phone number, your chosen route and any evidence. Appeals are hand-delivered or postmarked by the deadline. Late ones are not processed, and email or fax appeals are refused.

You pick one of three routes when you file:

  • Board of Equalization: free, three property owners with at least 40 hours of training. Either side can take the result to Superior Court within 30 days.
  • Nonbinding arbitration: you supply a certified appraisal dated within nine months before January 1, plus a $214 filing fee payable to the Clerk of Superior Court. The county refunds the fee if it accepts your appraisal.
  • Hearing officer: for value or uniformity disputes on non-homestead property or wireless personal property over $500,000, with no filing cost.

sections.h2: How do I claim a homestead exemption in Twiggs County?
sections.html:
Apply with the Board of Tax Assessors in Room 102 by April 1 of the first year you want the exemption. Georgia law requires that you own the house and use it as your primary residence, and failing to apply is treated as a waiver for that year.

The assessors also administer the Conservation Use Valuation Assessment and Forest Land Protection Act programs, which matter in a county where farms and timber dominate. These programs carry covenants, so ask for the commitment length before you enroll land you plan to sell soon. For current exemption amounts, call (478) 945-3663.

sections.h2: What should I do about taxes before selling a Twiggs County house?
sections.html:
Get a written payoff from the tax commissioner and match it to the settlement statement. Georgia bills the owner of record on January 1, so a late-year sale needs a clear split on paper between you and the buyer.

If you inherited land, ask for the history of every year you or the estate held it, since acreage in a shrinking county sometimes sits unpaid longer than a house in town. A bill unpaid more than 90 days after its due date can become a lien filed with the Clerk of Superior Court. Settling past years at closing clears the title for a buyer, whether that buyer finances or pays cash.

faqs.q: What is the phone number for the Twiggs County tax commissioner?
faqs.a: It is (478) 945-3359, at the Court House Square, 425 Railroad Street, Jeffersonville. The mailing address is P.O. Box 187.

faqs.q: How many days do I have to appeal a Twiggs County value?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date on the assessment notice. Appeals must be hand-delivered or postmarked by that date, and email or fax appeals are not accepted.

faqs.q: Does Twiggs County offer arbitration for appeals?
faqs.a: Yes. Nonbinding arbitration needs a certified appraisal and a $214 filing fee, and either side can later appeal the arbitrator's decision to Superior Court.

faqs.q: When is the homestead exemption deadline in Twiggs County?
faqs.a: April 1 of the year you want the exemption to start. Apply at the assessors' office in Room 102 of the courthouse.

faqs.q: Why does Twiggs County have so few building permits?
faqs.a: Census QuickFacts lists 13 permits for 2025 in a county of about 7,600 people. The county is rural, and population has fallen since 2020.
